BiblicalUsage: Mire is the word for mud, whitish clay — and it appears once, in the taunt against Zedekiah. In Jeremiah 38:22 the women left in the king's house shall say, thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back. One word, for a king stuck in the mud while his friends leave.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mire in Jeremiah is the end of bad counsel: the king's feet sink, and the friends who set him on are gone.
